title: Timeboxed deployment conductor for experiment schedulers
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a deployment conductor that supports timeboxed experiments, enforceable latency budgets and automatic failover/rollback when experiment SLAs are violated. Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRDs; console gets a new 'Experiments' tab.
description: Summary: Adds a new controller component (deployment-conductor) and supporting CRD fields to enable timeboxed, SLA-driven experiments for model rollouts. The conductor coordinates A/B and shadow experiments that are bounded by a wall-clock duration and enforce safe failover when latency or error budgets are exceeded. Motivation: teams running short-lived experiments (e.g., 15m promos, timed feature flags, limited traffic load tests) need deterministic, auditable experiments that automatically stop or rollback when their SLOs degrade. Existing rollout controllers support progressive percentages and metric gates but lack a compact primitive for timeboxed experiments with a unified failover policy. Design: - New CRD field: experiment.window {duration, traffic_fraction, latency_budget_ms, error_rate_threshold, aggressive_failover:boolean, postmortem_tag} - DeploymentConductor: watches Rollout CRs and Experiment sub-specs, creates ephemeral TrafficMirror/Shadow resources, enforces traffic caps, and sets timers for window expiration. - SLA enforcement: conductor samples P99 and tail error rates from the observability plugin and triggers immediate failover/rollback if observed metrics cross configured thresholds for more than 2 consecutive buckets. - Safe state transitions: conductor implements a three-state lifecycle: Scheduled -> Running -> Concluded (Succeeded|Failed|TimedOut). If 'aggressive_failover' is true, the conductor will cut traffic to the experiment target and route to the primary model immediately on fail; otherwise it will reduce by half and observe for a cooldown period. - Audit & observability: conductor emits ExperimentEvents and annotates the rollout trace with experiment_id and reason codes. Console adds an Experiments timeline for quick debugging. Compatibility and migration: existing Rollout CRs are not affected. New optional Experiment fields are ignored by older controllers. The system defaults to passive mode until experiment fields are present. Implementation notes and files changed (high level): - cmd/deployment-conductor/main.go: new binary + health, leader election, config parsing. - api/v1alpha1/rollout_types.go: experiment window fields and validation webhooks. - controllers/experiment_controller.go: core logic (scheduling, timer, metric sampling, enforcement). - internal/metrics/sampler.go: bucketed sampling used for SLA checks. - observability/events.go: experiment event types and wire format. - ui/src/experiments/ExperimentsPanel.tsx: front-end timeline and controls (feature-flag gated). - e2e/experiments/timeboxed_flow.test.ts: integration harness simulating latency regressions and ensuring rollback triggers. - charts/deployment-conductor/Chart.yaml + values.yaml: helm addition for Private/Dedicated deployments. Commits (summary): - feat: scaffold deployment-conductor binary and basic reconcile loop - feat: add Experiment window CRD and validation - feat: implement sampling and SLA check pipeline - feat: console UI for experiments (feature-flag controlled) - test: e2e timeboxed experiment flows with injected latency - docs: rollout guide and API reference for experiment window - fix: tighten leader-election to avoid double-schedule in HA clusters Highlights of important diffs (small illustrative snippets): - api/v1alpha1/rollout_types.go added: `ExperimentWindow struct { Duration string `json:"duration"` TrafficFraction float32 `json:"trafficFraction"` LatencyBudgetMs int `json:"latencyBudgetMs"` ErrorRateThreshold float32 `json:"errorRateThreshold"` AggressiveFailover bool `json:"aggressiveFailover"` }` - controllers/experiment_controller.go: sampling loop pseudocode included in comments for reviewer clarity. Testing and CI: - Unit tests for sampler and decision logic added. - Integration test simulates a P99 spike and asserts rollback within the configured budget window. - Flaky test: e2e/experiments/timeboxed_flow.test.ts occasionally failed when the fake-metrics-server experienced a race; CI rerun passed. Review conversation (selected threads): - Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Can we make the default cooldown window configurable cluster-wide rather than baked into the controller?" - Asha (author): "Added a top-level config value `experiment.cooldown_seconds` with a sensible default (60s). Documented in helm `values.yaml`." - Chen Li: "Sampling logic looks tight; verify memory use of sampler under high cardinality." - Asha: "Sampler uses fixed-size ring buffers per sample key (bounded by `sampler.max_keys` in config). Added tests to ensure GC behavior. See internal/metrics/sampler_test.go." - Morgan Reyes: "What guarantees do we provide for exactly-once scheduling in HA?" - Asha: "Leader election is enforced via the controller-runtime leader election built-in. I also added a lightweight scheduler lock in etcd (namespace-scoped) as a safety net if multiple controllers briefly think they're leader under partition. See controllers/scheduler_lock.go." - Reviewer approval flow: After two rounds of feedback (mainly configuration surface reductions and doc clarifications) Chen Li and Liam O'Connor approved. Merge and deployment notes: - CI green after rerun. - Manual canary: merged to main with squash; helm chart bumped to 0.8.1 and deployed to staging with `experiment.enabled=true`. - Observability: default 7d retention for experiment events; ops suggested increasing to 14d for compliance customers and a follow-up ticket was filed (ENG-6189). Rollout outcome and follow-ups: - This adds a new primitive for short-lived experiments used by product in a 15-minute promotional test. In staging, a deliberate latency injection triggered conductor failover within 32s of breach detection (within budget). - Follow-ups: UX polish on experiments timeline (PM DES-903), add automated smoke tests for console feature-flag, and provide a migration doc for clusters running older controllers (docs/experiments/migration.md). Linear links: ENG-6123 (conductor), ENG-6189 (observability retention follow-up).
